subject: Prompt set collection & model recommendations — ACME
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Josh Adams <josh.adams@acme.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Prompt set collection & model recommendations — ACME

Hi Josh —

Thanks again for taking the time today — great to hear more about ACME's customer support use cases and the handful of high-volume templates you outlined. Quick recap + next steps from our side: 

- Goal: reduce average handle time by surfacing suggested responses and classification labels for incoming support tickets (initial pilot ~5k tickets/day).
- Primary success metrics you mentioned: accuracy of top-1 suggested reply, latency under 200ms per suggestion, and cost per 1k requests.
- Key constraints: must remove or redact sensitive PII before sending to hosted inference (if you prefer private deployment we can discuss).

As discussed, two immediate asks we need from your team to kick off model-fit evals and prompt-set collection:
1) Share a representative set of customer prompts/examples (both common and edge cases). We provided a prompt_set_template.csv attached — please populate with 50–200 examples if possible and flag any that contain PII.
2) Highlight edge cases & failure modes you care most about (escalations, legal phrases, refunds/chargebacks).
3) Confirm whether ACME needs on-prem/private deployment for this pilot or if hosted with our redaction guidance is acceptable.

What we'll deliver after we receive the prompts:
- A short model-fit report with recommended model variants (quantized vs fp16) and benchmark links.
- A prompt/temperature sweep and a small eval harness comparing top-3 models on your prompt set and an edge-case slice.

I attached the prompt template and a small example CSV from a similar pilot for reference. Also linking our internal benchmark doc here: https://benchmarks.redwood.ai/acme-model-comparisons

Would it be possible to get the prompt examples by end of day Thu (Aug 20)? If that timeline is tight, let me know when procurement can turn around the sample data.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0143

Attachments: prompt_set_template.csv (CSV template), ACME_prompt_examples.csv (example, redacted)
From: Josh Adams <josh.adams@acme.com>

Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prompt set collection & model recommendations — ACME

Thanks Marissa — really helpful recap. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- We should be able to pull together ~100 examples from our ticketing system; procurement will handle any legal redactions before sending.
- Edge cases to flag: chargeback/refund requests, legal-ese (‘data breach’/‘GDPR’ mentions), and multi-turn threads that reference prior case IDs.
- On deployment: for the pilot the security team prefers hosted if we can guarantee automated PII redaction. If that doesn’t meet policy we’ll request a private deployment evaluation.

One question — for the evals: do you run both generation and classification benchmarks? We need both (classification for label suggestion, generation for reply drafts).

I’ll route the examples and attach notes from procurement — target to get you the CSV by Thu EOD.

—Josh

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prompt set collection & model recommendations — ACME

Josh — thanks, that sounds great. To answer your question: yes, we'll run both classification and generation benchmarks. Our deliverables will include:

- Classification: precision/recall on your labeled intents (top-label accuracy and F1), plus confusion matrix for edge-case slices.
- Generation: top-1 quality judgments on reply drafts using a small human eval set (we can do automated quality checks first and flag obvious regressions).

Preliminary model recommendations (based on similar customers & your latency/cost targets):
- For lowest latency and predictable cost: Redwood-XL-16Q (quantized variant) — best for high-throughput classification where final ranking happens server-side.
- For higher-quality generation (reply drafts): Redwood-2.7B-fp16 or gpt-compat-6B (depending on cost tolerance).

We'll run a quick sweep comparing these three (XL-16Q, 2.7B-fp16, gpt-compat-6B) and attach benchmark links once the eval is complete. Note on redaction: please follow the attached redaction guidance — if you can replace obvious PII with tokens (e.g., <EMAIL>, <SSN>) that helps our hosted eval pipeline. If redaction is not possible, we can sign an NDA + use the Private eval route.

If procurement wants a short writeup on data handling for the hosted evals, we can prepare a one-page summary for legal (SOC2 controls, encryption in transit & at rest). Logan — can you add the one-pager to the shared folder?

Thanks — will stand by for the CSV.

Best,
Marissa
